messages:
Maya: Pager P0 — large-scale routing cascade: hosted tenants accidentally routed to dedicated-quant variants in us-west-1 causing tokenization and KV-cache mismatches. IncidentBot: auto-created INC-2026-058 at 2026-03-25T09:19Z. Sam: oncall here, ack. Bridge up in #incident-bridge. Jin: I can see a huge spike of 'variant_incompatibility' in the router; policy 'cascade_fallback_v5' appears to have chosen dedicated variants when hosted pools were preferred. Log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-25T09:17:03Z] route_eval tenant=grocer-pro policy=cascade_fallback_v5 selected_variant=ded-quant-x10 reason=pool_capacity_fallback; inferred_compat=true
[2026-03-25T09:17:03Z] forward_to pool=dedicated-pool-21 shard=2
```
Sofia: CS reports grocer-pro & mall5000 with 25% failed requests, users seeing garbled text. Leo: MetricsBot shows regional fallback loops us-west-1 <-> eu-west-1 with retries amplifying between 09:17-09:22Z. MetricsBot: fallback spike us-west-1 = 5.5k/min peak.
Maya: timeline — cascade_fallback_v5 rollout began 09:14Z. Who deployed that? Jin: rollout by infra-cd, commit `e2b7c9a`. DeployBot: rollout job started 09:13Z and propagated to control planes.
Sam: mitigation plan: 1) pause cascade_fallback_v5 2) enforce explicit compatibility checks 3) throttle cross-pool spillover on edge to break retry amplification. Jin: pausing now:
```
$ rctl policy pause --name cascade_fallback_v5 --reason "emergency pause - misassigning hosted tenants to dedicated variants"
```
DeployBot: policy pause initiated (job jb-8105). Jin: adding guard to require explicit variant.compatible_with=="hosted":
```
$ rctl policy add-guard --policy cascade_fallback_v5 --expr "variant.compatible_with == 'hosted'"
```
IncidentBot: guard applied (g-1210). Leo: throttling spillover at the edge to 0 for us-west-1 to stop cross-region retry storms. Jin: running edge command:
```
$ rctl edge set-throttle --spillover-rate 0 --scope region:us-west-1
```
MetricsBot: after pause/throttle, fallback rate dropped from 5500/min to 140/min over 6 minutes. Error rate grocer-pro 09:17-09:22Z = 25% -> 09:28-09:40Z = 2.6%.
Sofia: CS notified affected accounts; Grocer-pro flagged for SLO impact. CustomerSuccessBot: grocer-pro CSM engaged and acknowledged.
Jin: root cause preliminary: variant metadata service had inconsistent compatibility flags due to a metadata migration that partially failed in eu-west shards earlier at ~09:00Z. The policy engine fell back to inferring compatibility from stale tags in the absence of an explicit flag. Migration logs:
```
[2026-03-25T09:00:11Z] metadata-migration apply variants_v3 -> partial_failure: shard eu-west-1 timeout; propagation incomplete
```
Sam: so cascade_fallback_v5 relied on inferred tags and that caused dedicated variants to appear compatible to hosted routes. Quick actions: rollback policy to cascade_fallback_v4 and invalidate caches. Jin: executing rollback and cache flush:
```
$ rctl policy rollback --name cascade_fallback_v5 --to cascade_fallback_v4 --reason "emergency revert - misroute via inferred compatibility"
$ rctl cache flush --keys tenant:grocer-pro,tenant:mall5000,variant:ded-quant-x10
```
DeployBot: rollback completed (jb-8110) at 09:25Z. Jin: cache flush acknowledged. Sam: remove sticky route entries and confirm clients' retries won't retrigger. Jin: removed sticky entries and added temporary short-circuit for tenants with tag 'hosted-only' -> force hosted pool.
Maya: infra-db, can you check why migration didn't propagate fully? infra-db: investigating — found throttling rule in metadata service that aborted propagation to eu-west shards when concurrent writes > 100; the migration hit a concurrency window and left inconsistent state.
Leo: long-term proposals: 1) policy engine must require explicit compatibility flags and fail-safe to prefer hosted pool on ambiguity 2) migration process must include a propagation check across regions before policy rollouts 3) add canary verification for variant metadata prior to promotion 4) add automatic circuit-breaker to stop repeated fallback loops.
Action items:
- Sam: postmortem owner and timeline + customer impact summary (SLO window and credit proposal)
- Jin: fix migration flow, add propagation verification + tests, and strengthen cache invalidation logic
- Leo: implement policy-engine default to prefer hosted on ambiguity and policy-level circuit-breaker for repeated fallbacks
- Sofia: customer follow-ups and SLO credit comms
- infra-db: remove/soften throttling rule or make migrations honor propagation checks
Participants: Maya, Sam, Jin, Leo, Sofia, IncidentBot, DeployBot, MetricsBot, CustomerSuccessBot, infra-db
Maya: will hold bridge until CS confirms no new errors for 20 minutes. Sam: will post final RCA in #postmortems and tag eng teams. Thanks for the quick response team :thumbsup:
IncidentBot: INC-2026-058 marked resolved at 09:39Z.
